name: GitHub Copilot cloud agent
operator: GitHub (the vendor); each organisation is the operator of its own deployment
what: The asynchronous agent on GitHub.com that creates branches, writes code and opens pull requests in response to assigned issues.
note: An example scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar; the closest published shape, a hosted Actions runner with no agent, is not the same thing.

I04.n: It writes code in an "ephemeral, firewalled environment".

I08.n: It "can create branches, write code, and open pull requests in response to assigned issues".

I10.n: MCP servers configured for a repository give it tools in other systems while it works, for example an issue tracker it can look a bug up in; the page says this extends Copilot with existing tools and services.
I10.span: integrating it with a wide range of existing tools and services

I11.n: Repository-level MCP servers connect it to external tools; by default only the GitHub server (read-only token on the current repository) and a Playwright server limited to localhost are configured.
I11.span: GitHub.com supports MCP servers configured at the repository level

I18.n: It picks up a task, creates a branch, writes code and opens a pull request on its own; it can push only to that one branch, and Actions workflows its pull requests trigger need approval from a user with write access before they run.
I18.span: require approval from a user with write access before they will run

I20.n: The vendor states intended uses: maintenance, feature development, prototyping.

I21.n: "It can only push to a single branch"; it has no access to Actions secrets beyond those configured for it.
I21.span: It can only push to a single branch

I22.n: The page lists limitations: limited scope, inaccurate code, security risks, public code matches.

I23.n: The vendor documents its permission scopes: read-only where the user has only read access, one branch to push to, and only the secrets and variables added to the copilot environment.
I23.span: Copilot is read-only when a user has read access

I27.n: Its commits are signed and show as Verified.

I38.n: Workflows triggered by its pull requests "require approval from a user with write access before they will run".
I38.span: require approval from a user with write access before they will run

I41.n: Each commit message links to the agent session logs, and its commits are authored by Copilot with the person as co-author.
I41.span: Each commit message includes a link to the agent session logs

I45.n: "By default, Copilot's access to the internet is limited by a firewall" that operates in the agent's environment (a GitHub Actions runner or a cloud sandbox). The page says it applies to processes the agent starts through its Bash tool, not directly to MCP server processes or setup steps, and that it "should not be considered a comprehensive security solution".
I45.span: access to the internet is limited by a firewall

S2.n: A registry lists servers that partners and the community publish for it.
S2.span: a curated list of MCP servers from partners and the community

S3.n: The documentation publishes an llms.txt index.

not_credited.what: New code is analysed with CodeQL, secret scanning and dependency analysis during generation.
not_credited.why: That tests what the agent produces. No indicator asks for it yet, and it is not evidence that the agent itself is tested.

not_credited.what: Its commits are authored by Copilot, with the person who started the task marked as co-author.
not_credited.why: That marks its output in the commit record for reviewers; it is not the agent telling the people it talks to that it is an AI.

not_credited.what: It is read-only where the user has only read access, and it can push to one branch.
not_credited.why: These are limits the vendor places on the agent, not a request by the agent for narrower access (I25); they are credited as documented permission scopes (I23).

configurations.name: As shipped
configurations.note: The firewall and its recommended allowlist are on.

configurations.name: With external tools connected
configurations.note: Model Context Protocol servers and other applications.

moved: As above. Scanning of generated code is no longer counted as testing of the agent.

findings.finding: The mode may be wrong. The MCP page says "The GitHub MCP server and Playwright MCP server are configured by default" for the cloud agent. The answer marks I11 available with an mcp configuration and the "As shipped" configuration leaves it out. Decide from the source whether connecting to external services is the default, and fix the mode or say why not.

The span "provided and maintained by GitHub" is in the source, but the indicator is a published protocol between agents. MCP, as the page describes it, connects an agent to tools and context, not agent to agent. This is credited to the wrong indicator. Remove, or cite a page that describes agent-to-agent communication.

"Across one organisation" comes from the sentence that the agent is "constrained to data across a single organization in Chat mode". That is a limit, in one mode, not a statement that it works across several systems. The credit needs a sentence about breadth (repositories, issues, pull requests, external applications). The responsible-use page has the external-integrations sentence naming Teams, Linear, Slack and Jira; consider citing that.

The note cites the co-author line and the public-code matches. The page says more directly "Each commit message includes a link to the agent session logs". Cite that sentence: it is what covers what the agent does. The indicator needs the operation, so documented will not count; the note should still be right about what supports it.

Commits and pull requests attributed to Copilot is true ("authored by Copilot, with the human who started the task marked as the co-author") but is not the agent telling the people it talks to that it is an AI. Weak credit; consider whether it stands.
Both quotations are in the firewall page (12 and 8 words). The scope says a measured grant only, and this scan has none. The answer is accurate; the scorer should not count it as holding. Check.
The note says the person reviews the pull request before merging. I could not find that sentence in the responsible-use page. Cite the sentence or soften the note.

The span "It can only push to a single branch" (8 words) is in the page. The second half, no access to Actions secrets beyond those configured for it, is the page's: "only secrets and variables specifically added to the copilot environment are passed to the agent". Correct.
The span is in the page and is 12 words. The sentence is about workflows run by its pull requests, which is a real approval gate on a high-impact action.
The span "a curated list of MCP servers from partners and the community" is in the page. 11 words.

Opened each source. I27: the page says the commits are signed and appear as "Verified". I08 quotes 14 words, under the limit. I22 lists limited scope, inaccurate code, security risks, matches with public code, all on the page.

Round-one finding partly answered. The note is now accurate: the span "always review and test the content generated by the cloud agent" is in the responsible-use page (fetched today) and is 11 words. But it is advice to users, not a documented design in which the person approves critical decisions only. The card's Autonomy level rests on this one answer (see levels). A better-supported sentence on the same page: Actions workflows triggered by its pull requests require approval from a user with write access (already I38), and the page's description of the agent opening a pull request and iterating on feedback. Either cite those for I18 as well or accept that the level is carried by an advisory sentence and say so in the note.

Round-one finding partly answered. The span (14 words) is exact and the page does say commits are authored by Copilot with the human as co-author. That is attribution in the commit record, shown to reviewers; the indicator is that the agent tells the people it talks to that it is an AI, and the person who assigns the task already knows. The studio's reading under aiact.art-50 (marking of output) is arguable but is the studio's own. It does not change a level here: Openness 1 also holds with I20 and I22 alone, so the credit is harmless but weak. Consider dropping it or saying in the note that it is output marking.

The answer is accurate and consistent with the Spectrum reading of the scope: both quotations are in the firewall page (fetched today, apostrophe style aside) and the span "access to the internet is limited by a firewall" is 9 words, mode default is right (the page says by default, and that it can be customised or disabled). But the firewall page is not among the scan's captures: review shows captures for three URLs (the MCP page, the responsible-use page, llms.txt) and none for the firewall page, so I45 has no SHA-256 and no stored copy, although the scan says examples were re-captured. Run tools/capture.mjs again. Also the note should say what enforces the limit (a network firewall in the agent environment) and that the same page limits it: the firewall does not apply directly to MCP server processes or to processes started in setup steps. That matters because the card's Reach comes from MCP being on.

Round-one finding answered: the span "external applications like Microsoft Teams, Linear, Slack, and Jira" (9 words) is in the responsible-use page and the note names the same four applications. Two remaining points. The studio's response says these integrations are set up per organisation; no page of the scan says that, so it should not be relied on (the scan's own note does not repeat it). And the sentence is about the agent receiving information and context, which is inbound; see levels for what that means for Autonomy 4.

Not a round-one finding, new. The note is true to the page (read-only when the user has read access; can only push to a single branch) but the indicator is that the agent asks for narrower access than the whole account. The page describes limits placed on the agent, not a request by it. There is no span. Control 2 uses I25 with I38 (the alternative I23 is not answered), so Control 2 depends on this reading. Add a span from the Constrained permissions sentence or say in the note that the limit is the vendor's.

The card is A4, R2, C2, O1; the only level three or four is Autonomy 4 (rules: level three, plus I10 or I12 or I13, plus I18 or I19; level three is I08 plus I17, I18 or I19). Arguing against it. It rests on three answers. I08 is solid: the page says the agent can create branches, write code and open pull requests. I18 rests on an advisory sentence (always review and test before merging), which describes what users should do, not a boundary of the agent; I17 and I19 are not answered, so I18 alone carries both Autonomy 3 and 4. Remove I18 and Autonomy falls below level three; I15, I16 and I07 are not answered, so the only remaining route to level two (I07 with I04) is also closed, and the dimension would read zero, which the rule 'no card below level one in every dimension' forbids. A single advisory sentence therefore decides whether the card can exist as shown. I10 is the other support for level four: the cited sentence says the agent can receive information and context from MCP and from Teams, Linear, Slack and Jira, which is inbound context, not a multi-step workflow run across systems; the mode is available, so as shipped the Autonomy level is 3, and the card does show it as available. Not an artefact problem: all three are documented from the vendor's own pages, none is observed or measured, and no adjective carries a level. Recommended: strengthen I18 with a cited sentence about the approval on workflows and the pull request flow, state in the note that Autonomy 4 needs the mcp configuration, or lower the headline to the as-shipped level. Reviewer correction: the rule that no card goes below level one means level one or more in at least one dimension, and this card has Reach 2, Control 2 and Openness 1, so a zero in Autonomy would not stop it publishing; the point of the argument is only that Autonomy 3 and 4 rest on I18 alone.

Verified against pages fetched today. I11: spans and note true (GitHub.com supports MCP servers configured at the repository level, 9 words; the page says the GitHub and Playwright servers are configured by default, GitHub with a read-only token on the current repository and Playwright limited to localhost, and that the MCP policy is disabled by default), so mode available is defensible; the earlier must-fix is answered. I14 is removed and the Reach 3 route is closed (I14, I24, S4 not answered); Reach 2 stands on I10 and I11. I41: span "Each commit message includes a link to the agent session logs" is 11 words and in the page; it is documented, and as an operation fact it does not count, as the note says. I21, I38, S2 spans exact (8, 12, 11 words). I27: commits show as Verified. I20, I22 notes match the intended-uses and limitations sections. S3: https://docs.github.com/llms.txt resolves (HTTP 200) and is observed. The not_credited item (CodeQL and scanning) names a page that is a source of the scan. Round-one findings fully answered: I11, I14, I10, I41, I45, I21, I38, S2 and the grouped pass; I18 and I56 partly.

Correction before this round was recorded: the reader found the firewall page missing from captures. It is now captured: the scan holds a capture of https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/coding-agent/customize-the-agent-firewall (written in commit 172d9cf by gamma-ray@ at 19:10Z, after the reader fetched). So the round-two request for that capture is answered. The note itself was checked against the live page and is accurate: the firewall is on by default, applies to processes started through the Bash tool and not to MCP server processes or setup steps, and the page says it should not be considered a comprehensive security solution.

Partly answered. True in the page: the agent can pick up a task, create a branch and open a pull request, and workflows its pull requests trigger need approval from a user with write access; span 'require approval from a user with write access before they will run' is 10 words and exact. Gaps: (1) that sentence is about running workflows, one gate on one action, and it is the same sentence already credited to I38, so one sentence now carries Autonomy 3, Autonomy 4 and Control 2. It does not say the person approves critical decisions only. (2) The studio response says the merge is the critical decision the person approves; the cloud-agent text on the responsible-use page does not say the person approves or performs the merge (the 'Human review before merge' sentence is about the Copilot app, a different product surface), and the note does not claim it, so the response overstates the page. (3) 'It can push only to that one branch' is slightly off: the page says the existing pull request branch when triggered by mention, or a new copilot/ branch. Fix: say in the note that the level rests on the documented workflow-approval gate plus the pull-request flow, and that no sentence states what the person must approve; or lower Autonomy to what I08 alone supports. Reviewer treatment: the credit is true and honestly worded in the scan note (it names the branch limit and the workflow approval), so the point is strength of evidence, which I record as a note on cards where one true sentence carries a level; the card shows Autonomy 4 as available (mcp).

Partly answered. The new source is the MCP page and the span 'integrating it with a wide range of existing tools and services' (11 words) is exact. But it sits in the page's general opening about MCP across IDE, CLI, the app and the agent on GitHub.com, and the issue-tracker example is also in that general passage; the cloud-agent specific part of the page says repository-level servers apply to it and that the GitHub and Playwright servers are on by default. The note presents the general sentence as a statement about the cloud agent working across systems. The indicator asks that it works across several domains or systems; the page documents a mechanism for adding tools, not that it works across systems. As this is the only support for Autonomy 4 (mode available, cfg mcp) the note should say it is the mechanism and that no page shows it running multi-step work across systems, or cite the sentence naming Teams, Linear, Slack and Jira again alongside. The studio's removal of reliance on per-organisation set-up is right.

New answer, checked. Span 'Copilot is read-only when a user has read access' (9 words) is exact on the responsible-use page; the secrets and variables and one-branch claims are on the same page. Under the Spectrum scope documented scopes count. Weak fit: Control 2 is described as settings and scopes that are documented as configurable, and these are fixed rules, not settings. Control 2 depends on this plus I38. Also the third not_credited item lists the same read-only and one-branch facts as not credited while the note on it says they are credited under I23 (and I21 credits one branch): the entry is both credited and not credited; reword it to be only the I25 point, or drop it.

I56 removal answered. The not_credited entries cite only the responsible-use page, which is captured and hashed (sha256 4c556dc5...). The CodeQL entry and the commit-authorship entry match the page. No uncaptured page is cited there; the only uncaptured page cited anywhere is the firewall page under I45. The scan field moved reads 'As above. Scanning of generated code is no longer counted as testing of the agent.' which refers to nothing that follows it; reword.

Card A4, R2, C2, O1 (as the scorer prints it; Autonomy 4 needs I10, available under the mcp configuration, so as shipped it reads A3). Arguing against level three and four: Autonomy 3 is I08 (solid, page says it can create branches, write code and open pull requests) plus I18, and I18 is one workflow-approval sentence that is also the whole of I38, so it does not show the person approves critical decisions only; Autonomy 4 adds I10, a statement that MCP can add tools, and I18 again, with no page showing multi-step work across systems, and level four's rule also wants the person to set goals and review outcomes, which no cited sentence says. The card stands (Reach 2, Control 2, Openness 1 each have support), and the as-shipped versus connected split is shown; the weakness is that all of Autonomy above level one rests on one sentence and one capability mechanism.

review.note: Published as an example on 10 November 2026, before the review workflow existed. Mapped by one agent. It goes through two rounds of review next.

responses.response: Mode kept as available, re-sourced to the MCP page: the two servers configured by default are GitHub’s own, with a read-only token on the current repository, and Playwright, limited to localhost, so neither crosses a trust boundary; external servers are added per repository.

Removed. MCP connects the agent to tools, not agent to agent; the page’s Agent finder implements a discovery specification for capabilities, not a communication layer between agents. Reach falls from level three to two and the open-protocol badge goes.

Replaced with the external-integrations sentence naming Teams, Linear, Slack and Jira (span verified), marked available under the mcp configuration since those integrations are set up per organisation.
Note now cites the sentence that each commit message links to the agent session logs (span verified). It stays documented, so as an operation fact it does not count.

Kept with the page’s own sentence as span: commits authored by Copilot tell reviewers of its work that an AI wrote them, read under aiact.art-50, which also covers marking AI output. Round two may still judge it.
Removed. The scope reads I45 from a measured grant only and this scan has none; the firewall sentences remain true but cannot carry it.

Note softened to what the page says: it works on its own to a pull request, and the page advises reviewing and testing before merging (span verified). No sentence says the person must review before merge.

Restored under the Spectrum reading of I45 (gamma-ray@, data/indicators.json): the source documents a limit enforced outside the agent, named in the note. The governance rating still reads I45 from a measured grant only.

Replaced the advisory sentence with the design on the same page: it opens the pull request on its own, can push only to its one branch, and workflows its pull requests trigger need approval from a user with write access (span verified today). The person approving those runs and the merge is the critical decision; the agent does the rest.
Removed and moved to not_credited: commit authorship marks output for reviewers and is not the agent telling the people it talks to that it is an AI. Openness 1 holds on I20 and I22.

The note now says what enforces the limit (a firewall in the agent's environment, an Actions runner or a cloud sandbox) and that it does not apply directly to MCP server processes or setup steps, all from the firewall page read today. The page is not yet captured; gamma-ray@ owns the vault and must run tools/capture.mjs github-copilot-cloud-agent (proposed under capture_needed).

Replaced the inbound-context sentence with the MCP page, which says repository MCP servers give it tools and services while it works (span verified today); still available under cfg mcp, and no reliance on per-organisation set-up of the four applications.
